thread.title_full: Durable medical equipment drives $489,729 in Medicaid spending in Monroeville for 2024

author: H. M. Forsythe
title: Durable medical equipment drives $489,729 in Medicaid spending in Monroeville for 2024
text:
Monroeville Medicaid providers billed $489,729 for services within the Durable Medical Equipment category in 2024, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database shows. This amount reflects a 48.9% rise compared to 2023, when providers filed $329,008 in claims for this service group.
Medicaid, a public health insurance program administered by states and funded through both federal and state dollars, covers low-income individuals and families, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities. The program is a significant component of the U.S. health care system.
Since Medicaid spending comes from taxpayers, trends in local claims offer insights into how health care funding is distributed in each community.
The “Durable Medical Equipment” category encompasses a range of Medicaid-billed services defined by specific standardized HCPCS and CPT code groupings. For this report, each billing code was assigned to a single service category according to uniform code prefixes and numerical groupings, grouping related services while avoiding duplication and supporting accurate trend analysis.
Durable Medical Equipment was eighth in total Medicaid spending among service categories in Monroeville for 2024, even as several categories experienced overall increases.
Statewide in Pennsylvania, Durable Medical Equipment also held the number eight spot for total Medicaid payments during 2024.
Across the five years leading up to 2024, Medicaid payments assigned to the Durable Medical Equipment category in Monroeville grew by $412,455, an increase of 533.8%. Some periods saw especially strong growth, including 2020 and 2021.
Spending for Durable Medical Equipment was distributed throughout Monroeville but mainly concentrated in a few ZIP codes. In 2024, the ZIP code 15146 accounted for $489,728 in Medicaid payments for the category, representing 100% of all such spending locally that year.
Within the Durable Medical Equipment category, claims were further concentrated within a small set of billing codes.
Between 2024 and 2023, Medicaid spending for Durable Medical Equipment in Monroeville climbed by 48.9%, whereas the overall change across all Medicaid claim categories in the city was 20.4% for the same period.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data shows combined state and federal Medicaid payments totaled about $871.7 billion in fiscal 2023, making up around 18% of the nation’s total health care expenditures. That’s up from $613.5 billion in 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.
This 40% increase over several years is attributed mainly to both enrollment growth and increased use of services during and after the pandemic.
Recent federal budget bills passed under the Trump administration introduced major changes to Medicaid’s funding. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,”, signed in 2025, is expected to trim more than $1 trillion in federal Medicaid spending over the next 10 years and includes policies such as work requirements and higher out-of-pocket costs for some recipients. These adjustments are likely to put additional pressure on state budgets and may slow future growth in federal Medicaid contributions, even as the program remains essential for tens of millions of Americans.
